text: This video shows a doeff handler choosing a move by running battle itself. doeff is algebraic effects for Python.
We look at battle, the card fight, and the handler monte_carlo, as it answers one Choose.
The fight pauses at a Choose. The handler holds the rest of the fight as k.
To answer, it runs battle itself: the same function a person plays. It needs no model of the game.
For each card it can play, and for ending the turn, it plays that card on the state. Then it starts a new battle from that state, three times.
Each new battle runs on a stack of its own. None of them touches k, so the paused fight keeps its dice.
The handler counts the wins. Here every move wins all three. The paused fight has not moved.
With a tie it keeps the first move, Bash. It resumes k with it, once: in doeff, k can be resumed only one time. The fight goes on.
On seed 3, the bot answers eleven Chooses with a hundred and sixty-five playouts, in about a fifth of a second.
